## 18. Final gate

Required V1.42 gate:

```text
V1.42_RESOLUTION_CACHE_LIFETIME_GATE: PASS
```

The gate proves:

- zero production cache owners;
- zero production resolver consumers;
- no renderer/scene resolver path;
- no production fingerprint persistence consumer;
- diagnostic frame reuse is miss-once/hit-after;
- shared exact-identity reuse exists;
- equal-budget distinct graphs show no hidden cross-scene correctness issue;
- `ResolutionFingerprint.cache_identity` remains the identity;
- COLOR boundary remains unchanged.

## 19. Next step — V1.43

V1.42 should **not** be followed by another speculative cache manager.

The next checkpoint should be driven by the first real consumer integration if/when one appears.

### V1.43 micro-scope

1. identify the first actual production caller of `resolve_component()`;
2. map its object owner and destruction boundary;
3. determine whether it is renderer-, scene-, shot-, frame- or request-owned;
4. pass a real caller-owned `ResolutionCache` through that boundary;
5. measure actual frame reuse rather than the V1.42 diagnostic loop;
6. measure actual scene cardinality from the real owner;
7. measure actual retained memory and LRU churn;
8. test teardown of the real owner;
9. compare shared/partitioned behavior using actual simultaneous scenes;
10. only add partitioning if measured LRU pollution requires it;
11. only add byte budgeting if real memory evidence requires it;
12. only add persistence if a restart/persistent consumer exists;
13. rerun V1.39–V1.42 cross-surface and concurrency gates;
14. preserve `ResolutionFingerprint.cache_identity` as the only semantic cache identity;
15. preserve the COLOR boundary unless a distinct real consumer is independently proven.

If no real consumer appears, V1.43 should remain an audit/architecture checkpoint rather than inventing an orchestration layer.
